## Plan

### Mechanics summary
- Kin Priest (190 HP) with Kin Followers (58–59 HP each) `[GAME-EXTRACT]`. At A10 on v0.111.1: Priest 199 max HP, followers 62 and 63 `[OBS]` (live state, 2026-11-19; all three started 9 below max because of a start-of-combat relic). The simulator still uses the extract's numbers.
- **Followers:** Quick Slash 5, Boomerang 2×2, Power Dance +2 Strength.
- **Priest:** Orb of Frailty 8 + Frail, Orb of Weakness 8 + Weak, Beam 3×3, Ritual +2 Strength.
- Everyone gains Strength over time. The longest Act 1 boss fight (median 9 turns).

### Deck checklist
- **Countable checks** (`tools/deck_check.py`, tuned on the history 2026-11-19) `[PLAYER-DATA, weak]`: powers at least 1 (the longest Act 1 fight; survived 1.0, fatal 0.4); hit-all attacks at least 1 (followers stack Strength (plan)).
- **Hit-all damage is good here** (unlike against Vantom): Breakthrough, Thunderclap, Whirlwind, Conflagration, Pact's End, Stomp, Howl from Beyond.
- **The wiki** `[COMMUNITY]` (slaythespire.wiki.gg page, accessed 2026-11-19) confirms the cycles (Priest: Orb of Frailty 8 + Frail, Orb of Weakness 8 + Weak, Soul Beam 3×3, Dark Ritual +2 Strength; followers: Quick Slash 5, Boomerang 2×2, Power Dance +2 Strength) and adds that the two followers are offset: one starts with Quick Slash, the other with Power Dance. Their Minion power reads "Minions abandon combat without their leader."
- **Killing the Priest ends the fight** `[GAME]`: the in-game Minion tooltip on the followers reads "Minions abandon combat without their leader" (seen live on v0.111.1, A10, 2026-11-19), and the Player has ended the fight this way before `[PLAYER-SAID]`. Two guides (gamerblurb and selphie1999gaming, accessed 2026-11-19) said the same `[COMMUNITY]`. They disagree on the default line: race the Priest if it can fall in 2–3 turns, otherwise clear the followers first.
- **Simulated targeting** `[HYPOTHESIS]` model (`reports/phase2/vantom-simulation.md`; far too hard for this boss in absolute terms, 1% from 60/80 against the Player's 8 of 8): with a single-target deck, sending every attack at the Priest won 38% against 31% for the planner's own targets; with two hit-all cards (Thunderclap, Conflagration) the planner's targets, which clear the followers, won 77% against 63% for racing. Hit-all cards were worth far more here than against any other boss.
- **Kill order** `[HYPOTHESIS]`: followers first if hit-all damage can clear them in 2–3 turns (they stack Strength). Otherwise race the Priest. The followers carry **Minion** (`MINION_POWER`: their deaths are not "fatal" for the encounter) `[GAME-EXTRACT]`, which strongly suggests that **killing the Priest ends the fight**, as with minions in the first game `[HYPOTHESIS]`, to confirm. If it holds, racing the Priest (190 HP) is usually right unless hit-all damage clears all followers within 2 turns. `tools/plan_turn.py` treats a plan that kills every non-minion (here the Priest) as lethal, so it will show the race when it is on (gap 12 confirms or refutes this).
- Frail and Weak come every cycle. Expect lower block and damage on those turns.

### HP target on arrival
- Ironclad benchmark: median 34.5, p75 41.2. **Rest if HP is below about 45.** Fatal fights started much lower (41% against 64%, all characters).

### First three turns
- Clear followers with hit-all cards while their Strength is low. Block the Priest's orbs.

### Potion plan
- Hit-all damage potions early. Block potions late, when everyone has Strength.

### What killed the Player here, and the counter
- Ironclad: 0 of 8 fatal (all characters: 5 of 28). The deaths came with low arrival HP. `[PLAYER-DATA]`
- Counter: arrive healthy; bring hit-all damage.
